title: Technical English — Course 5, Semester 1 — Pilot Variant 12

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the configuration lesson take place?
tasks.audioText: The configuration management tutor will review equipment identification on Monday at ten thirty. Students should bring the configuration list and the model-reference sheet. The lesson will compare model designation, serial number and installed option codes. The tutor will explain why the equipment identity must be clear before technical data are selected.
options: At ten thirty on Monday
At nine thirty on Monday
At ten thirty on Tuesday
At eleven thirty on Monday

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which two maintenance records are required for the aircraft task review?
tasks.audioText: The configuration management tutor will review equipment identification on Monday at ten thirty. Students should bring the configuration list and the model-reference sheet. The lesson will compare model designation, serial number and installed option codes. The tutor will explain why the equipment identity must be clear before technical data are selected.
options: The serial-number register and equipment-status report
The configuration list and model-reference sheet

tasks.prompt: Configuration identification describes the specific model and installed options of an item of equipment. A model designation alone may not show every difference between individual units. Serial numbers and option records can provide additional detail. Technical information should be selected only after the relevant configuration has been established, particularly when similar models have different installed equipment. Reading 1. Why may a model designation alone be insufficient?
options: Because the model designation is always incorrect
Because serial numbers are used only for delivery records
It may not show all differences between individual units
Because installed options are identical across all models

tasks.prompt: What should happen before technical information is selected?
options: Select a manual using the model name alone
Use the information from the nearest available unit
Assume that all installed options match the standard model
The relevant configuration should be established

tasks.prompt: The equipment configuration ___ before the technical data are selected.
options: must be established
must establish
establishing
are established

tasks.prompt: Choose TWO identifiers that may help distinguish individual equipment configurations.
options: The colour of the storage shelf
The operator's favourite manufacturer
Serial number
Installed option record

tasks.prompt: The particular arrangement of installed equipment and options is a configuration ___.
Two units have the same model designation but different options. What should you ask?
options: The model designation is enough.
Could we check the serial number and installed option record before selecting the data?
The option record can be ignored.
I will use the first manual I find.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of configuration identification in a logical order.
options: Review installed options
Identify the model designation
Select technical information for the confirmed configuration
Check the serial number
correctOrder: Select technical information for the confirmed configuration

tasks.prompt: Write 100–120 words explaining why model, serial number and installed options should be checked before using technical information.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total. Score each criterion 0–2: (1) Identification — 2: explains checking model and serial number against the actual equipment/asset; 1: partial; 0: absent. (2) Configuration — 2: explains checking installed options or configuration differences; 1: partial; 0: absent. (3) Technical-data match — 2: explains verifying that the information applies to that identity/configuration and seeking confirmation if uncertain; 1: partial; 0: absent or unsafe. (4) English — 2: clear explanation and accurate technical vocabulary; 1: errors but meaning clear; 0: meaning frequently unclear.
